requirements.statement: Ticket admission must consume a paid issued unused event-scoped ticket at most once with its audit in the same transaction; inventory holds must respect tier/event capacity; accepted transfer must rotate the credential and revoke former-holder projection. Checkout quantity must not exceed the approved versioned per-order limit; approved/retired commercial policies cannot regress to draft or lose immutable history. Approved tax-inclusive pricing must preserve advertised integer totals for every accepted quantity, conserve total = organizer payable + platform fees + tax, and retain the purchased mode immutably; an event-specific tax rate is independently authorized. An unresolved signed-provider refund or reversal bound to the same checkout/capture/merchant must fence admission even when legacy rows still say paid and issued. PayPal capture requires an authenticated readback of the original provider order, with unchanged internal-order, merchant, amount and currency validation before marking paid. Zero platform fees must create no zero-valued ledger entry while cash, organizer payable, tax and nonzero fees conserve the captured total. A verified external refund/reversal received before capture binding leaves durable merchant-scoped evidence after inbox retry exhaustion; later binding must fence admission without a webhook replay. Canonical orders reject legacy bulk status mutations. Refund routing follows the unique succeeded provider, retaining existing non-PayPal request behavior. Retained issued tickets of partially refunded orders remain transferable under the purchased policy. OAuth failure before a refund POST leaves the request retryable; ambiguous POST outcomes retain the no-repeat fence. Accepted provider refund identities survive mismatched monetary responses so exact authenticated readback can reconcile without another POST. Whole-ticket partial refunds accept any eligible subset matching the stable cent allocation. An authorized guest order receipt remains accessible when public ticket sales close; receipt lookup failure must not offer a replacement purchase.
requirements.openReason: Approved current-main implementation is incorporated with explicit traceability; exact consolidated tests and deployment remain outstanding.
ambiguities: Provider payment, real delivery, recipient age acknowledgment, exact event activation and offline/staff delegation remain separate gates.

requirements.statement: A public consent request must not activate WhatsApp consent. It records a pending request; claiming a confirmation request is one conditional update allowed only when the number has no request in the last 24 hours, and simultaneous first requests for a number do not fail. A request the provider did not accept stays pending as undelivered: for 1 hour from the request the number can still confirm it by messaging first and a new public request may retry the send without changing the request instant; afterwards it waits for the 24-hour interval. Delivered requests to a number are therefore at least 23 hours apart. Consent becomes active only through one conditional update when the same number sends an affirmative keyword whose Meta message timestamp is no earlier than the pending request, within 7 days of a delivered request, and the request has not been withdrawn since; a concurrent withdrawal wins and a delayed or replayed earlier reply cannot confirm a newer request. The confirmation request uses the approved template named by WHATSAPP_CONSENT_TEMPLATE when configured; the person may also message SI first (VITE_WHATSAPP_OPTIN_URL). Public responses never disclose a number's consent state; the public consent lookup returns 410 without reading consent data. Opt-out (public form, inbound STOP/SALIR/BAJA/CANCELAR or staff revocation) always withdraws consent and invalidates any pending request without resetting the 24-hour interval, and its stored instant is never earlier than the request it defeats; neither withdrawing, confirming nor staff capture lets anyone request another message early. The public opt-out notifies only a number that was subscribed. The failure of a superseded send attempt changes nothing. Staff consent capture remains admin-only.
requirements.openReason: Bounded model, unit and PostgreSQL tests pass on the candidate; not deployed, and production has no WhatsApp Cloud API configuration to exercise it.
ambiguities: Affirmative keywords are exact single-word matches; free-text consent is not inferred.

OpenAPI still documents a 200 response for GET /public/whatsapp/consent and the previous POST description; correcting it regenerates the web and Mobile clients and is deferred to the next Mobile client regeneration.

Production has no WhatsApp Cloud API configuration (WHATSAPP_TOKEN, WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID, WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN), so no confirmation can be sent or received until it is configured; an approved template (WHATSAPP_CONSENT_TEMPLATE) is required for business-initiated requests outside a 24-hour window.
The 1-hour window for an undelivered request is an engineering default chosen because the number never saw a prompt; the product owner has not confirmed the duration.
A provider failure that hides an actual delivery (ambiguous timeout) is treated as undelivered and could allow a second request inside the interval.

A withdrawn request cannot be replaced until 24 hours after its request instant. Because opting out needs no proof of control, a third party can impose that wait on someone else's pending request; this is accepted so that the unauthenticated opt-out cannot be used to message a number repeatedly. Staff capture remains available.
An undelivered request that is neither confirmed nor retried within 1 hour waits for the 24-hour interval even though nothing was delivered.

requirements.statement: A music purchase order references one rule, release version and price in integer minor units and opens a commerce checkout session in the music_download domain. Only server-verified provider evidence bound to the order marks it paid; triggers then grant exactly one entitlement and end it on refund or chargeback. Entitled and free downloads use the same downloadable-asset predicate, count each new request identifier against the entitlement limit, answer a repeated identifier only while its signed URL is valid, and issue URLs that live 300 seconds. A free grant that was revoked is not revived by a new request.
requirements.openReason: Payment record, entitlement and download rules are modeled within bounds and exercised on PostgreSQL; provider calls are untested and several failure-path defects are open. Commerce is disabled by default and should stay disabled until they are closed.
ambiguities: No live payment provider wiring for music_download has been verified.
Music payments bypass the shared payment runtime and the production provider switches; only the commerce flag for the checkout environment gates them.

A recorded provider failure cancels the order irreversibly while the payment may still complete, and an entitlement can end up active on a cancelled order; repair needs a trigger migration and a product decision.
A failure after the provider charged leaves no reconciliation record; no webhook or reconciliation path exists for this domain.
Partial refunds keep the entitlement and disputes revoke it permanently; both need a product decision.
Download limits count authorizations, not transferred bytes; one counted download gives access for just under 600 seconds.
